title: Fewest Refuelling Stops
statement:
A car drives along a straight road from position `0` to position `target`. It uses **1 unit of fuel per 1 unit of distance** and starts with `start_fuel` units. Each entry `[position, fuel]` in `stations` is a fuel station at that position that gives **all** of its `fuel` units if you stop there. The stations are listed in increasing order of position, and every position is between `1` and `target - 1`.

The tank has no size limit. You may refuel at a station you reach with an empty tank, and arriving at `target` with an empty tank counts as arriving. Return the **smallest number of stops** needed to reach `target`, or `-1` if it cannot be done.
constraints: 1 <= fuel <= 1000000000 for every station; positions are strictly increasing
sums can exceed a 32-bit integer: use 64-bit numbers

examples.explanation: Stop at 8 (fuel 20) and at 30 (fuel 25): the car can then reach 8 + ... in all 12 + 20 + 25 = 57 >= 50. One stop is not enough: 12 + 20 = 32 < 50.
Even using both stations the car can drive only 10 + 3 + 2 = 15 units.

hints.nudge: You do not have to decide at a station whether to stop. What if you could decide LATER, looking back at all the stations you passed?
hints.pattern: Greedy with a max-heap: drive as far as the fuel allows, remembering the fuel of every station you pass; when you get stuck, 'retroactively' refuel at the passed station with the most fuel.
hints.pseudocode:
reach = start_fuel; stops = 0; i = 0; heap = empty max-heap
while reach < target:
  push the fuel of every station with position <= reach (advance i)
  if heap is empty: return -1
  reach += pop the largest fuel; stops += 1
return stops
hints.walkthrough: A DP over (stop count -> furthest reach) works in O(n^2). A faster idea: `reach` is how far you can drive with what you have taken so far. All stations at or before `reach` are stations you could have stopped at. When `reach` is not yet the target, you must have refuelled once more, and to get the furthest you should have used the passed station with the MOST fuel. A max-heap holds the fuel of the stations you passed and have not used. Repeat: add every newly reachable station to the heap, take the largest, add it to `reach`, count one stop. If the heap is empty while `reach` is still short of the target, you are stuck: return -1. Use 64-bit numbers for `reach`.
